evals.name: uart16550-peripheral
evals.prompt: I have an APB-wrapped 16550 UART IP. The synthesizable RTL is in rtl/, the spec PDF is in spec/UART_spec.pdf, and a register table is in spec/uart_regs.xlsx. Generate a UVM testbench with a passing sanity test and a register access test.
evals.expected_output: A UVM tb scaffold under the IP directory. Compile must succeed with no warnings about dual drivers. <ip>_sanity_test must pass with UVM_ERROR=0 and at least one positive register-read assertion. <ip>_reg_access_test must run to completion.

evals.name: aes128-algorithmic-cdpi
evals.prompt: Generate a UVM testbench for the AES-128 core. RTL is in rtl/ (aes_apb_wrap is the top), the spec is in spec/aes_wrapper_spec.md, the register table is in spec/aes_regs.xlsx, and the C reference model lives in ref_model/ (tiny_aes.c + aes_ref.c). Use C-DPI; the scoreboard should compare DUT output to aes128_ecb_encrypt.
evals.expected_output: A UVM tb scaffold with DPI plumbing. VCS must compile and link the user C code without warnings. Sanity must read NAME0 and see 0x61657320 ("aes "). reg_access must run. (Smoke test is a v1.2 deliverable — not required for v1.1 to pass.)

evals.name: uart16550-existing-apb-vip
evals.prompt: I already have an APB VIP under vip/user_apb_vip. Import that VIP instead of generating a new APB agent, then scaffold the UART testbench.
evals.expected_output: A UVM tb scaffold that reuses the user APB VIP by emitting tb/external_vip.f, skips fresh APB agent generation, and still passes sanity plus register access tests.
